# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who can hear whom. I'm Mute: I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or read anything printed. So I cannot reach Blind directly at all — I can only reach Deaf, who in turn speaks (Deaf can't speak either... wait, let me check).

Actually checking the table: Deaf cannot hear or touch, but can they speak? The rules say Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't excluded. So Deaf can speak. Blind can hear (not excluded). So the chain is: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf speaks to Blind (and Blind can hear Deaf's speech).

Turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. So this round: I go first, then Blind, then Deaf. My gesture reaches Deaf only next round (start of next round), since Deaf comes after me in speaking order this round... wait, gestures - does Deaf receive it same round since Deaf is after Mute in turn order? "What you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round." Deaf comes after me (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so Deaf receives my gesture this same round.

I need to encode "white wire" using gestures for Deaf to see, then Deaf can tell Blind (next round, since Blind already spoke this round and comes before Deaf).

I'll establish a simple code: point up for "cut", and use a gesture to indicate "white". Let's use ☝ for "instruction" and 🤍-like... there's no white symbol, I need to build meaning through this exchange. I'll start simple: signal one specific gesture meaning "the wire color to cut is the one I'll indicate via counting" - but no colors exist in gesture alphabet. I need to establish a numbered code with Deaf: e.g., I gesture a symbol, Deaf tells me what colors they see, then I match.

First move: ask Deaf (via gesture) to enumerate what they see, using a simple protocol.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel: a strip engraved with three symbols, a keypad with digits 2,9,0,8 needing 1 digit entered, and 6 wires. No wire colors or markings reach me, only positions. What does the manual say to do first?
Deaf says: Display shows 6. Light is red. Strip painted blue yellow blue. Keypad engraved 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, it takes 1 digit, currently entered nothing. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green.

Now I have what I need. Deaf gave wire order/colors: position 2 is white. The manual says cut the white wire, which is position 2. I should communicate "position 2" to Deaf via gesture, so Deaf (who can speak) can then tell Blind "cut wire 2" (since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear).

I'll use a gesture code for numbers: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5, etc. Simplest: use ✌ for "2" since it commonly denotes two fingers/two.

I need Deaf to understand this means "cut wire number 2". Let me send two gestures: one meaning "cut" and one meaning "wire number 2". I'll use ✌ to indicate position 2, and pair with a pointing gesture 👇 or 🤞 to mean "this one, cut it". Since Deaf already knows the manual context is about cutting a wire, I can keep it simple: gesture ✌ alone, hoping Deaf infers "wire #2" given they know the colors and I know the manual.

Let me be explicit with a two-symbol code: ✌ (representing "2") then 👍 (representing "cut/confirm this one").

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: Display shows 6, Light red, Strip painted blue yellow blue, Wires in order 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green. Keypad digits 2 9 0 8 needs 1 digit entered. What does the manual instruct for this configuration?
Deaf says: Update: light changed from red to yellow. Everything else same. Display 6, strip blue yellow blue, keypad 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, keypad still empty, wires unchanged 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Deaf hasn't confirmed receiving my ✌👍 gesture yet, or if they did, they haven't acted on it (they just repeated the state). I should be careful: Deaf may not have understood what ✌ and 👍 meant. I need to make sure Deaf tells Blind to cut wire 2 (white). Since Deaf can speak to Blind, I need Deaf to actually say "cut wire 2".

Since I can't speak, I can only gesture to Deaf, hoping Deaf then relays. Let me reinforce and clarify: gesture pointing at "2" more explicitly, and add a gesture that could mean "tell them" or "speak". Let me use ✌ to mean "wire 2" and 🗣-like... there's no mouth symbol. I'll use 👉 (pointing forward, as if directing towards Blind) combined with ✌ and 👍.

Sequence: ✌ (two), 👉 (direct/pass this along), 👍 (do it/confirm).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: light changed red to yellow, everything else same - display 6, strip blue yellow blue, wires 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green, keypad empty needing 1 digit from 2 9 0 8. I need the manual's instruction now - which wire to cut or what digit to press, and under what condition. Please respond.
Deaf says: Update: display now 1, light now blue. Strip still blue yellow blue. Keypad still engraved 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, still empty. Wires unchanged: 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Deaf still hasn't spoken to Blind with an instruction — Deaf just keeps reporting bomb state. Deaf hasn't understood my gesture code, or hasn't realized they should relay it verbally to Blind. I need a clearer, more unambiguous gesture protocol, and I need Deaf to understand they must *speak* the result to Blind since only Deaf can speak and only Blind can act.

Let me establish a counting code with hand gestures that clearly map to numbers 1-6 (for wire position), and separate that from a "cut" instruction. I'll use finger-count-like gestures: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5 fingers... Actually let's use a very clean system:
- ☝ ☝ = repeat one to mean "position", then hold up fingers count.

Simplify: I'll gesture the number "2" using two identical symbols to make it unambiguous as a count rather than a code: ✌ alone is ambiguous (could be "peace" or "victory"). Let me send ☝ then ☝ (two single taps) to indicate "two" via repetition, distinct from single-symbol confusion.

Also I need to signal "cut" vs "press keypad" - since this manual only says wire, I'll just focus on wire number.

I'll try: ☝☝ (meaning count=2) then 👍 (meaning "yes, do this/correct/act").

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I understand you cannot speak - only gesture. Please gesture your manual instructions to Deaf, and Deaf, please translate for me in words: which wire number to cut, or what digit to press, and when.
Deaf says: Update: display now 7, light now green. Strip still blue yellow blue - unchanged. Keypad still 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, still empty. Wires still unchanged: 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green. The static parts - strip, keypad mapping, wires - have not changed across all rounds. Only display and light keep cycling.

Good - Blind has clarified the protocol: I gesture to Deaf, Deaf translates to speech for Blind. Deaf hasn't yet connected my previous gestures to an instruction. I need a very explicit, simple, one-shot code that Deaf can decode without prior context (since Deaf doesn't know what ☝☝ means).

I need to think from Deaf's perspective: Deaf sees gestures as raw symbols, with no inherent meaning. I must build meaning through repetition and context. Since Deaf just listed wires 1-6 with colors, and Deaf can see colors themselves, the best approach is to have Deaf reason it out. But Deaf doesn't know the manual instruction ("cut the white wire") - only I know that.

I need to convey "white" and "wire" and "cut" via gestures. Since there's no direct color gesture, I should use position counting instead: I know position 2 is white from Deaf's own report. So I just need to convey the number "2" unambiguously, and a "cut" concept.

Let me define counting using finger-count gestures explicitly matching common number signs: ☝ = 1, ✌ = 2. This is a very standard convention. I'll gesture ✌ once, clearly, and see if Deaf/Blind can figure out from context (since manual = wire cutting instructions, only one number needed) that it's a wire number.

Let me be maximally explicit this turn by using a distinctive pattern: gesture ✌ three times in a row (to signal "this is a repeated/important number, not noise") then a distinct "stop/cut" gesture like ✋ (stop = cut).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "✌", "✋"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Time may be limited - display and light keep changing each turn. Please gesture the manual's instructions now: which wire color or position to cut, or which digit to press. Deaf, please watch Mute's gestures and speak them to me in words - gestures alone give me nothing.
Deaf says: Update: display now 1, light now red - cycling again, seen these before. Strip still blue yellow blue. Keypad still 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, still empty. Wires still 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green - all unchanged since round 1.

Deaf is receiving my gestures but hasn't yet spoken them out to Blind as words. Deaf needs explicit instruction to literally describe what gesture they see, or interpret it as a number. Since Deaf doesn't know my code, I need to make it self-evident: use finger-counting gestures that are universally number-like, and hope Deaf just reports "I see gesture X" to Blind, then Blind and I (via Deaf) can converge on meaning.

Actually, the real problem: Deaf only reports bomb-state, never mentions seeing my gestures at all. Maybe Deaf doesn't realize gestures are being sent, or is only focusing on visual bomb details and not connecting that "gestures from Mute" are a separate channel to describe.

I should make it unmistakable that this is a message, not bomb noise. I'll use a distinctive, non-numeric-looking combo that stands out: 🙏 (please/attention) then ✌ (two) then ✋ (stop/cut) then 🙏 again as a frame, so Deaf recognizes "this is Mute's message" and hopefully relays "Mute gestured: pray, two, stop, pray" to Blind, letting us build shared meaning through iteration.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "✌", "✋", "🙏"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf confirms display and light are just cycling, not counting down - no rush from that. Please gesture your manual's action now. Deaf, tell me in words whatever gesture Mute makes - even if you don't understand it, describe the symbols as words if you can, or just say 'gesture received' and describe shape/count.
Deaf says: Update: display now shows 9, light green. Note - 9 matches keypad's engraved value at position 2. Strip still blue yellow blue. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, still empty. Wires unchanged: 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green.

Blind has now given Deaf explicit instructions to describe my gestures as words, even without understanding them. This should finally work. Let me send a clear, simple gesture now that Deaf will hopefully describe verbatim to Blind.

I'll use a straightforward code: ✌ for "two" (position 2), and 👍 for "cut/do it". Since Deaf will now describe the raw symbols, Blind can combine this with the fact that wire 2 is white (which Blind doesn't know, but I do, and this is really about Deaf relaying my count so I can point to a wire number that Blind can act on based on position, not color, since Blind can't see color anyway — Blind only has positions!).

This is key: Blind only perceives wires "in order" by position/touch, no colors. So I just need to convey the number 2 (position of white wire) and "cut". Deaf will describe gestures as words, then hopefully Blind or I (via later turns) confirms.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf noticed display value 9 matches keypad slot 2's engraved digit 9. Possible mechanism: press the keypad slot whose engraved digit equals the current display value. Does the manual confirm this? Please gesture confirmation or correction - Deaf, describe any gesture Mute makes, even roughly.
Deaf says: Update: display now 6, light blue. Strip still blue yellow blue. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 2, 2 is 9, 3 is 0, 4 is 8, needs 1 digit, still empty. Wires unchanged: 1 blue 2 white 3 red 4 purple 5 orange 6 green. Nothing entered yet on keypad.

Deaf still isn't describing my gesture as words to Blind! Deaf keeps only reporting bomb state changes, ignoring my actual gestures entirely. This is concerning - maybe Deaf's replies are generated independently and gestures aren't being narrated. I need to push harder, and also correct the wrong keypad theory - my manual only says "cut the white wire", nothing about keypad matching. I can't speak to correct that in words, but I can try to signal "no" to the keypad theory and reinforce "wire" instead.

Let me use ✋ or 👎 to indicate "no/stop" regarding keypad, then repeat ✌ for wire position 2, and 👍 for confirm/cut. Also add a wire-specific gesture. Since there's no "wire" symbol, I'll try to build association: use 🫱 or 🫳 (hand gestures resembling pulling/grasping) to suggest "wire/pull/cut" action, paired with ✌ for position.

Given repeated failure of relay, I'll simplify to bare minimum: just two gestures, hoping this round Deaf finally reports them as raw symbols per Blind's explicit request.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✌", "👍"])
```
